entries.title: Lenses: drivers around the search core
entries.text: For plan:connect4-exact, budget ∘ null_window ∘ core, as game.rs nests them (the drawing follows the current plan as pieces are dropped or removed): each driver is a frame whose left band carries its two lanes; inside, the alpha-beta core turns a position into children, ranks them with the order chain (small lenses on the move-list lane) and turns child values back into a max/min with cutoffs. The memo is a lens inside the core: its get feeds the forward pass, its store is fed by the backward pass. Dashed loops are state a backward pass leaves for a later forward pass (the table for tt_best, history for history). The recursion and the leaf, where values come from, close the right end.

entries.title: The core: the alpha-beta search
entries.text: The search is fixed (alpha-beta over Game); a plan chooses what swaps in. As a box it is Position → Value⊥, and it has one typed hole per SearchPlan field. Fail-soft alpha-beta in the +1 side's view: inside the bounds every result is a bound on the true value; with the window the whole range, it is the value (game.rs:590-592). It is not a piece. It reads and writes the transposition table and lends the history table to the chain; no plan field names it, because plan.rs fixes the search and a plan picks what swaps in.

entries.title: ∅ → N ← ∅: both feet empty
entries.text: The fixture declares no ports: every place is interior, so each foot is the empty set. A closed net is an open net with empty feet, ∅ → N ← ∅. Gluing along ∅ is only the disjoint union: there is nothing to identify. Nothing on its boundary can be glued: no place is exposed.

entries.title: N : 0 → 0: nothing to synchronise
entries.text: The Connect-4 net declares no ports, so neither boundary has a port to synchronise on. Def. 4.1 with m = n = 0: a P/T net with no ports is a net with boundaries N : 0 → 0 (Remark 3.6 says so for C/E nets, and that composing two of them is their disjoint union). Remark 3.11: a net N : 0 → 0 has no boundary, so there is no way of interacting with it. The fixture is a plain P/T net (no inhibitor arcs, no capacities), so Def. 4.1 applies as stated.

entries.title: The plan runs over N; it is not glued to it
entries.text: The plan runs over N: SearchPlan::solver(&Game) builds a solver for a game on this net. It is not glued to it: the plan has no places. A SearchPlan is the pieces of the game search, picked by name. Its slots are filled by pieces; plan.rs's check decides what fits. It composes by chaining, wrapping and filling, which is the operad view's subject. Composite: none. N is closed (∅ → N ← ∅), and a plan is not a net, so there is no pushout to draw here.

entries.title: Slot: the order chain
entries.text: SearchPlan field "order". Takes Order pieces, chained (≤ 8, none twice): a monoid under ++, [] the identity. Absent, the chain is Chain::default (order.rs:205-216: tt_best, immediate_win, history). Order never changes a value, only how soon a cutoff comes: reordering changes node counts, never the value (order.rs:1-7). The empty chain: every key ties and the moves keep the net's own order (order.rs:197-199); it is the monoid's identity, not the default chain. The chain is compared piece by piece, the first to differ decides; a decisive piece's nonzero key settles the rank, so decisive pieces that lead the chain form a top tier (order.rs:26-31, 249-265). The ROADMAP's law: every composite stays ct:order-only.

entries.title: The laws that must fail do fail
entries.text: The order chain does not commute (NOT_chains_commute fails, as it must); its value does (value_ignores_order, from the assumed rule order_only, order.rs:4-6). null_window and budget do not commute in the theory (NOT_drivers_commute fails, as it must). "order": [] is the unit of chain (rules unitL, unitR); it is not the absent key, which is Chain::default() (RESULTS.md, mismatch 3). The rules are readings of order.rs and plan.rs, marked ASSUMED; Chyp checks that each rewrite follows from them.

entries.title: C cannot see the win detectors' reads
entries.text: C forgets read arcs, inhibitor arcs and self-loops (pre = post). The Connect-4 win detectors' reads of the board do not show in C: a win detector takes a cell and puts it back (pre = post = 1), which C records as 0. The fixture declares no invariants, so no y·C check is drawn.
